claims.claim_text: CITE-seq analysis of DC-enriched PBMCs from 12 Atlanta cohort subjects (5 healthy controls and 7 COVID-19 patients sampled at day 2, 8, 9, 9, 15, 15, and 16 after symptom onset) showed an early transient interferon-stimulated gene signature including IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15 in COVID-19, despite absent detectable IFN-α and IFN-β gene expression.

source.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15 (see C11-C MONO_IFN and C18-T_IFN in fig. S10). These IFN response–enriched clusters emerged only in samples from COVID-19 patients (fig. S12).

comparison.finding: COVID-19 samples showed an early transient interferon-stimulated gene signature including IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15, with IFN response–enriched T-cell and monocyte clusters emerging only in COVID-19 patients, despite absent detectable IFN-α and IFN-β gene expression.

claims.claim_text: Bulk RNA seq analysis of PBMCs from an extended Atlanta cohort of 17 healthy controls and 17 COVID-19 samples showed strong induction of the 33-gene CITE-seq-derived ISG signature in COVID-19 versus healthy donors, while IFN-α and IFN-β transcripts were not detected.

source.quote: We observed a strong induction of the ISGs in COVID-19 subjects compared with healthy donors in this dataset as well ( Fig. 4G ). Of note, we did not detect expression of genes encoding IFN-α or IFN-β, consistent with the CITE-seq and flow cytometry experiments ( Fig. 4D and Fig. 2 , respectively).

comparison.finding: strong induction of the 33-gene CITE-seq-derived ISG signature in COVID-19 versus healthy donors; IFN-α and IFN-β transcripts were not detected

claims.claim_text: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls across the Hong Kong and Atlanta cohorts showed significantly reduced plasmacytoid dendritic cell frequencies and reduced pS6 in pDCs with decreased IκBα in mDCs in infected individuals versus healthy controls.

source.quote: There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts ( Fig. 1C ).

comparison.finding: COVID-19 patients had significantly reduced plasmacytoid dendritic cell frequencies, reduced pS6 in pDCs, and decreased IκBα in mDCs versus healthy controls

claims.claim_text: Flow cytometry of ex vivo stimulated PBMCs from the Atlanta cohort (14 healthy and 17 COVID-19 donors) showed reduced IFN-α and TNF-α production by pDCs and reduced IL-6 and TNF-α responses by mDCs to viral or bacterial TLR ligand cocktails in infected individuals versus healthy controls.

source.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls ( Fig. 2A ). The TNF-α response was also significantly reduced in the pDCs of infected individuals, which demonstrates that the pDCs are functionally impaired in COVID-19 infection.

comparison.finding: infected individuals had reduced IFN-α and TNF-α production by pDCs and reduced IL-6 and TNF-α responses by mDCs to viral or bacterial TLR ligand cocktails versus healthy controls

claims.claim_text: O-link analysis of plasma from the Atlanta cohort showed that 43 cytokines were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 versus healthy controls, with TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and oncostatin M showing strong positive associations with clinical severity and TNFSF14 elevated in COVID-19 but not influenza or RSV.

source.quote: Of the 92 analytes measured, 71 proteins were detected within the dynamic range of the assay. Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection ( Fig. 3 , top row, and fig. S6).

comparison.finding: 43 cytokines were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 versus healthy controls, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10; TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and oncostatin M were significantly enhanced in COVID-19 infection
TNFSF14 was elevated in COVID-19 but not influenza
TNFSF14 was elevated in COVID-19 but not RSV

claims.claim_text: Q-PCR analysis of plasma from 18 healthy and 51 infected individuals showed significantly higher bacterial DNA, measured as bacterial 16S rRNA gene product, in severe and ICU COVID-19 patients versus healthy controls.

source.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product, and of LPS, as measured by a TLR4-based reporter assay ( Fig. 6, A and B ).

comparison.finding: severe and ICU COVID-19 patients had significantly higher bacterial DNA, measured as bacterial 16S rRNA gene product, than healthy controls
